capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Pack stated as 77.4 kWh (bare capacity recorded as gross); SlashGear relays Hyundai's 77.4 kWh for the US car.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: European listing of the same 77.4 kWh pack (MY22): 74.0 kWh usable. Pack is shared across markets.

chemistry.notes: EV Database: NMC cathode, pouch. Wikipedia lists the 77.4 kWh pack as NMC too.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 697 V nominal, 800 V architecture.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: electrive (2023) and Hyundai Motor Group (2023 IONIQ 5) describe automatic navigation-triggered battery conditioning with no manual control; the 2022 service bulletin TSB 23-01-017H adds the same navigation trigger to 2022 cars by software update. Applied to the whole 2022-2024 first generation (same E-GMP hardware); later Hyundai manuals add a manual option, but nothing found says the 2022-2024 cars have it. Caveats: no source was found for 2024 specifically (extended from 2023); electrive says the feature "arrived with" the 2023 model year and reached older cars by software update, so a 2022 car without that update may have no battery conditioning.

dc_max_kw.notes: Wikipedia and EV Database list 233 kW peak for the 77.4 kWh pack (European/global figure; Electrek says the 2025 US car's 257 kW is "up from 233 kW in prior years").

ac_max_kw.notes: Canada Drives (Canadian 2022 trims): 10.9 kW onboard charger, standard on all models; SlashGear gives the same for the US car.

published_10_80_min.notes: Hyundai: 10-80% in 18 minutes on a 350 kW charger (relayed).
